title: Which data integration tool fits you?

questions.hint: Self-run tools have no software fee, but you pay for servers and staff time.

options.label: A vendor runs it for me
options.why: you want a vendor to run the pipelines

options.label: My team runs it on our own servers
Pipelines should live as code in Git
options.why: you want pipelines kept as code

options.label: I live inside AWS or Azure
options.why: you work inside AWS or Azure, where the post lists Glue and Azure Data Factory

questions.q: What are most of your sources?

options.label: SaaS apps such as Salesforce
options.why: you load many SaaS apps, and OLake Go reads databases, Kafka and S3

options.label: Databases that need fresh data
options.why: you need database changes with fresh data

options.label: Old systems under governance rules
options.why: you have older systems or governance rules, and Qlik lists mainframe connectivity on Enterprise

options.label: Mostly SQL, REST APIs and files
options.why: you load SQL databases, APIs and files

questions.q: How fresh must the data be?

options.label: Within minutes
options.why: you need database changes within minutes

options.label: A warehouse
options.why: you load a warehouse, and OLake Go writes Iceberg and Parquet

options.label: Iceberg tables
options.why: you want Iceberg tables, which shrinks the field to the writers in the post's second table

questions.q: Does your data have to stay in your network?

options.label: Yes, I need to host it myself
options.why: you want to host it yourself: Airbyte Core, Meltano, dlt and OLake Go run on your own servers, and Informatica, Qlik and Estuary list self-run options

options.label: No, a hosted service is fine
options.why: a hosted service is fine for you, so vendor-run tools stay in play

fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A vendor-run tool with a big connector list, billed on monthly active rows per connection.
fivetran.bestWhen: nobody wants to run pipelines and your sources are mostly SaaS.
fivetran.watchOut: Oracle, SAP and Db2 (Beta) sources are only on Enterprise and Business Critical, and since January 2026 deleted rows count as paid MAR.

hevo.name: Hevo
hevo.summary: A managed tool with a free plan and entry prices you can see.
hevo.bestWhen: you want a managed tool with a small, published price.
hevo.watchOut: streaming must be enabled through sales, Iceberg is Early Access and Snowflake-managed only, and we found no self-hosted edition.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: A big connector list you can self-host as Core or rent as Cloud.
airbyte.bestWhen: you want lots of connectors and the option to self-host.
airbyte.watchOut: syncs are scheduled, not continuous (its pricing page lists 1 hour on Standard, 15 minutes on Plus and 5 minutes on Pro and Enterprise Flex), and Core uses the Elastic License 2.0, which does not let you sell a cloud service that gives users direct access to Airbyte.

estuary.name: Estuary
estuary.summary: Streaming and batch from one tool, with real-time capture from several databases.
estuary.bestWhen: you need fresh data and per-connector fees do not scare you.
estuary.watchOut: its Iceberg connector needs AWS EMR Serverless and S3, and each connector instance adds a monthly fee.

qlik.name: Qlik Talend Cloud
qlik.summary: Log-based CDC and Iceberg from one vendor, bought by quote.
qlik.bestWhen: you need CDC from older systems into Iceberg and are fine buying by quote.
qlik.watchOut: no dollar price is published, and the Starter edition has no CDC.

informatica.name: Informatica
informatica.summary: A large suite for governance and big, mixed estates.
informatica.bestWhen: you need governance and a big mixed estate.
informatica.watchOut: we found no dollar price per IPU on its site, so you need a quote, and its database ingestion docs describe Iceberg only as Snowflake-managed tables.

glue.name: AWS Glue
glue.summary: A serverless AWS service for Spark jobs that writes Iceberg to S3.
glue.bestWhen: your team writes Spark and lives on AWS.
glue.watchOut: we found no log-based CDC engine documented for Glue ETL jobs, and jobs need storage and a catalog as well.

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: An open-source tool that captures Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB and SQL Server changes into Iceberg or Parquet on storage you own.
olake.bestWhen: you run your own infrastructure and want database changes in Iceberg tables.
olake.watchOut: it reads databases, Kafka and S3 rather than SaaS apps, and it does not transform data.

code.name: Meltano or dlt
code.summary: Free code-first tools: Meltano keeps pipelines in Git, and dlt is a Python library.
code.bestWhen: your team likes code and wants control.
code.watchOut: you own scheduling, upgrades and on-call work, we found no official Meltano Iceberg loader, and the log-based option we found in dlt's open-source docs is Postgres.

adf.name: Azure Data Factory
adf.summary: Microsoft's managed ETL and ELT service, billed on activity runs, copy hours and data flow hours.
adf.watchOut: native CDC covers SAP, Azure SQL, SQL Server, Cosmos DB and Snowflake, and its Copy activity writes Iceberg only to Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2.
